name: Elimelech's family loses husband and sons in Moab
summary: Famine drives Elimelech, his wife Naomi, and their two sons from Bethlehem to Moab; Elimelech dies there, the sons marry the Moabite women Orpah and Ruth, and after about ten years both sons also die, leaving Naomi without husband or sons.

name: Ruth vows to stay with Naomi
summary: When Naomi urges her widowed daughters-in-law to return to their own people, Orpah kisses Naomi goodbye and leaves, but Ruth clings to her and vows never to leave her, pledging herself to Naomi's people and her God.

name: Naomi returns to Bethlehem and asks to be called Mara
summary: Naomi and Ruth arrive in Bethlehem at the start of barley harvest, stirring the whole town, and Naomi tells the women to call her Mara instead, because the Almighty has dealt bitterly with her.

name: Ruth gleans in Boaz's field
summary: Ruth goes out to glean leftover grain to support Naomi and happens to end up in the field belonging to Boaz, a worthy man from the clan of Naomi's dead husband Elimelech.

name: Boaz shows Ruth favor and provision
summary: Boaz notices Ruth, tells her to stay close to his young women and share his workers' water and food, and instructs his reapers to pull grain from the bundles and leave it for her to glean.

name: Naomi identifies Boaz as a family redeemer
summary: Ruth brings home about an ephah of barley, and when Naomi learns whose field she gleaned in, she tells Ruth that Boaz is a close relative and one of their family redeemers.

name: Naomi instructs Ruth to approach Boaz at the threshing floor
summary: Naomi tells Ruth to wash, anoint herself, and go down to the threshing floor that night, wait until Boaz has finished eating and lain down, then uncover his feet and lie there until he tells her what to do.

name: Ruth asks Boaz to be her redeemer
shortName: Ruth's request at the threshing floor
summary: Startled awake at midnight to find Ruth lying at his feet, Boaz learns her identity and hears her ask him, as a family redeemer, to spread his garment over her.

name: Boaz names a nearer redeemer and sends Ruth home with barley
summary: Boaz blesses Ruth for not seeking a younger man, tells her a relative nearer than himself must be given first chance to redeem her, and sends her back to Naomi before dawn with six measures of barley.

name: The nearer redeemer forfeits his right to Boaz
summary: At the town gate before ten elders, Boaz offers the nearer redeemer the right to buy Elimelech's land; once told the purchase requires marrying Ruth to preserve the family name, the man declines and transfers his right to Boaz by removing his sandal.

name: Boaz marries Ruth and the elders bless them
summary: Boaz takes Ruth as his wife before the elders and people at the gate, who bless the marriage and pray that Ruth will be like Rachel and Leah, who built up the house of Israel.

name: Ruth bears Obed, grandfather of David
summary: Ruth bears a son named Obed, whom Naomi nurses as her own, and the closing genealogy traces his line from Perez through Boaz down to Jesse and David.
